title.zh: 卷五 魏書五 后妃傳
title.en: Volume 5: Book of Wei 5 - Biographies of empresses and concubines
title.raw: 卷五 魏書五 后妃傳 Volume 5: Book of Wei 5 - Biographies of empresses and concubines

sentences.zh: 易稱「男正位乎外，女正位乎內；

translations.literal: The Changes says, "The man takes the correct position outside, the woman takes the correct position inside;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says that the man belongs in the outer sphere and the woman in the inner sphere;

sentences.zh: 男女正，天地之大義也」。

translations.literal: when man and woman are correct, it is the great righteousness of heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: when each stands in the right relation, that is the great moral order of heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不明后妃之制，順天地之德，故二妃嬪媯，虞道克隆，任、姒配姬，周室用熈，廢興存亡，恆此之由。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings all clarified the regulations for empresses and consorts and complied with the virtue of heaven and earth; therefore the two consorts married into the Gui clan, and the way of Yu flourished; Ren and Si were paired with the Ji house, and the Zhou house thereby prospered—rise and fall, survival and perdition constantly stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every wise king of antiquity made clear the rules governing empresses and concubines and aligned them with the moral pattern of heaven and earth. Hence the two royal brides who joined the Gui line made Yao’s line thrive, while Ren and Si, wed into the Ji clan, brought radiance to Zhou. Whether a state flourishes or fails has almost always turned on this.

sentences.zh: 春秋說云天子十二女，諸侯九女，考之情理，不易之典也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn exegesis says the Son of Heaven has twelve women and a feudal lord nine women; examined against human reason, this is an unchanging norm.
translations.idiomatic: Exegetical tradition on the Spring and Autumn Annals assigns twelve consorts to the Son of Heaven and nine to a feudal lord; weighed by common sense, that norm has not changed.

sentences.zh: 而末世奢縱，肆其侈欲，至使男女怨曠，感動和氣，惟色是崇，不本淑懿，故風教陵遲而大綱毀泯，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet in degenerate ages men grew extravagant and unrestrained, indulging their lavish desires until men and women were left resentful and long separated, disturbing the harmonious qi; they honored only physical beauty and did not root conduct in virtuous grace, so customs and instruction declined and the great bonds were ruined and lost—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, however, rulers gave themselves to excess and appetite until men and women languished apart in bitterness, unsettling the harmonious air of the realm. They exalted mere loveliness instead of grounding choice in true goodness, until morals frayed and the fundamental ties of society collapsed. What a waste.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，有國有家者，其可以永鑒矣！

translations.literal: Alas—those who possess a state or a family may take this as a mirror forever!
translations.idiomatic: Alas: any who would hold a realm or a household ought to keep this lesson before them always.

sentences.zh: 漢制，帝祖母曰太皇太后，帝母曰皇太后，帝妃曰皇后，其餘內官十有四等。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations the emperor’s grandmother was called Grand Empress Dowager, the emperor’s mother Empress Dowager, the emperor’s consort Empress, and the remaining inner-palace offices numbered fourteen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Han law styled the sovereign’s grandmother Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, his chief consort Empress, and recognized fourteen grades of inner-court women below them.

sentences.zh: 魏因漢法，母后之號皆如舊制，自夫人以下，世有增損。

translations.literal: Wei followed Han law; titles for the empress dowager and the like all matched the old system; from the rank of Lady downward, each generation saw additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adopted Han precedent: the titles of the empress’s mother and similar ranks stayed as before, while from Lady downward successive reigns added or pruned offices.

sentences.zh: 太祖建國，始命王后，其下五等：有夫人，有昭儀，有倢伃，有容華，有美人。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor founded the state he first appointed a queen; below her were five grades: there was Lady, there was Brilliant Companion, there was Handmaid of Favor, there was Graceful Splendor, and there was Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao established his kingdom he first set a queen above five grades: Lady, Brilliant Companion, Handmaid of Favor, Graceful Splendor, and Beauty.

sentences.zh: 文帝增貴嬪、淑媛、脩容、順成、良人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen added Honored Concubine, Virtuous Lady, Cultivated Countenance, Accomplished Success, and Good Woman.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di expanded the roster with Honored Concubine, Virtuous Lady, Cultivated Countenance, Accomplished Success, and Good Woman.

sentences.zh: 明帝增淑妃、昭華、脩儀；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming added Virtuous Consort, Splendid Companion, and Cultivated Deportment;
translations.idiomatic: Ming-di added Virtuous Consort, Splendid Companion, and Cultured Bearing;

sentences.zh: 除順成官。

translations.literal: he abolished the office of Accomplished Success.
translations.idiomatic: and he abolished the Accomplished Success post.

sentences.zh: 太和中始復命夫人，登其位於淑妃之上。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he again ordered the rank of Lady and placed it above Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe the court restored the title Lady and set it above Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 自夫人以下爵凡十二等：貴嬪、夫人，位次皇后，爵無所視；

translations.literal: From Lady downward the noble ranks totaled twelve grades: Honored Concubine and Lady ranked next after the queen and had no parallel for their noble rank;
translations.idiomatic: Below the empress came twelve noble grades. Honored Concubine and Lady stood immediately beneath her, with no exact analogue among outside nobility;

sentences.zh: 淑妃位視相國，爵比諸侯王；

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort’s position was equated to the Chancellor and her noble rank compared to a feudal prince;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort’s salary matched the Chancellor’s and her fief ranked with a prince of the blood;

sentences.zh: 淑媛位視御史大夫，爵比縣公；

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady’s position was equated to the Imperial Counselor and her noble rank compared to a county duke;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady matched the Imperial Counselor and ranked with a county duke;

sentences.zh: 昭儀比縣侯；

translations.literal: Brilliant Companion was compared to a county marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant Companion matched a county marquis;

sentences.zh: 昭華比鄉侯；

translations.literal: Splendid Companion was compared to a village marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Companion matched a village marquis;

sentences.zh: 脩容比亭侯；

translations.literal: Cultivated Countenance was compared to a pavilion marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated Countenance matched a pavilion marquis;

sentences.zh: 脩儀比關內侯；

translations.literal: Cultivated Deportment was compared to a marquis within the passes;
translations.idiomatic: Cultured Bearing matched a marquis-within-the-passes;

sentences.zh: 倢伃視中二千石；

translations.literal: Handmaid of Favor was equated to two thousand shi at the full rate;
translations.idiomatic: Handmaid of Favor drew pay like a full two-thousand-shi official;

sentences.zh: 容華視真二千石；

translations.literal: Graceful Splendor was equated to two thousand shi at the true rate;
translations.idiomatic: Graceful Splendor drew true two-thousand-shi rank;

sentences.zh: 美人視比二千石；

translations.literal: Beauty was equated to two thousand shi by comparison;
translations.idiomatic: Beauty compared to two-thousand-shi salary;

sentences.zh: 良人視千石。

translations.literal: Good Woman was equated to one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Good Woman matched one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 武宣卞皇后

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan of the martial and manifest virtue, née Bian
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan (the martial and manifest empress), surnamed Bian

sentences.zh: 武宣卞皇后，琅邪開陽人，文帝母也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, née Bian, was a native of Kaiyang in Langye and was Emperor Wen’s mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bian, posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, came from Kaiyang in Langye and was Cao Pi’s mother.

sentences.zh: 本倡家，

translations.literal: Her family had been entertainers by profession.
translations.idiomatic: She was born into a family of performers.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后以漢延熹三年十二月己巳生齊郡白亭，有黃氣滿室移日。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: The empress was born on the jisi day of the twelfth month of the third year of Han’s Yanxi era at White Pavilion in Qi commandery, and yellow qi filled the chamber for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records that she was born on jisi in the twelfth month of Han Yanxi 3 at White Pavilion in Qi, while yellow vapor filled the room for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 父敬侯怪之，以問卜者王旦，旦曰：「此吉祥也。」〉

translations.literal: Her father the Marquis of Respect wondered at it and asked the diviner Wang Dan, who said, "This is auspicious."〉
translations.idiomatic: Her father, ennobled as the Respectful Marquis, was troubled and questioned the diviner Wang Dan, who answered, “This is a blessed omen.”〉

sentences.zh: 年二十，太祖於譙納后爲妾。

translations.literal: At age twenty the Grand Progenitor took her as a concubine at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: When she was twenty, Cao Cao took her as a concubine at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 後隨太祖至洛。

translations.literal: Later she followed the Grand Progenitor to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She later accompanied him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及董卓爲亂，太祖微服東出避難。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo threw the realm into chaos the Grand Progenitor went out east in disguise to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo’s rebellion convulsed the capital, Cao Cao slipped away in plain clothes toward the east.

sentences.zh: 袁術傳太祖凶問，時太祖左右至洛者皆欲歸，后止之曰：「曹君吉凶未可知，今日還家，明日若在，何靣目復相見也？

translations.literal: Yuan Shu spread word that the Grand Progenitor had died; those of his attendants who had reached Luoyang all wished to return, but the empress stopped them, saying, "We do not yet know whether Lord Cao is alive or dead; if we go home today and he is alive tomorrow, with what face could we meet him again?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu circulated a false report of Cao Cao’s death. His followers in Luoyang wanted to flee homeward, but Lady Bian told them, “You cannot know yet whether my lord lives or dies. If you leave today and he proves alive tomorrow, how could you bear to look him in the eye?

sentences.zh: 正使禍至，共死何苦！

translations.literal: Even if disaster comes, what hardship is there in dying together!
translations.idiomatic: Even if the worst comes, is dying together so terrible?

sentences.zh: 」遂從后言。

translations.literal: " So they followed the empress’s words.
translations.idiomatic: ” They stayed because she said so.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而善之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor heard of it he praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heard the story and approved her steadiness.

sentences.zh: 建安初，丁夫人廢，遂以后爲繼室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jian’an era Lady Ding was set aside, and he then made the empress his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jian’an, after Lady Ding was cast off, he made Lady Bian his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 諸子無母者，太祖皆令后養之。

translations.literal: For sons who lacked mothers the Grand Progenitor ordered the empress to rear them all.
translations.idiomatic: He told her to raise every motherless son of his household.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖始有丁夫人，又劉夫人生子脩及清河長公主。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: At first the Grand Progenitor had Lady Ding, and Lady Liu bore sons Xiu and the Princess of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary adds that Cao Cao first had Lady Ding, while Lady Liu bore Cao Ang and the Princess of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 劉早終，丁養子脩。

translations.literal: Lady Liu died early, and Lady Ding raised son Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu died young, and Lady Ding reared Cao Ang as her own.

sentences.zh: 子脩亡於穰，丁常言：「將我兒殺之，都不復念！

translations.literal: When son Xiu perished at Rang, Lady Ding kept saying, "You killed my son; you never think of me again!
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Ang died at Rang, Lady Ding cried again and again, “You got my son killed and spare me no thought at all!

sentences.zh: 」遂哭泣無節。

translations.literal: " Then she wept without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: ” and she wept without measure.

sentences.zh: 太祖忿之，遣歸家，欲其意折。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor grew angry, sent her home, and intended her resolve to break.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cao Cao sent her back to her family, expecting her resolve to crumble.

sentences.zh: 後太祖就見之，夫人方織，外人傳云「公至」，夫人踞機如故。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Progenitor went to see her; the lady was weaving, and when outsiders announced "The lord has come" she sat astride the loom as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went to visit. She was at her loom; when servants cried that the lord had arrived she stayed seated as she was.

sentences.zh: 太祖到，撫其背曰：「顧我共載歸乎！

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived he stroked her back and said, "Will you not ride home with me!
translations.idiomatic: He stepped in, laid a hand on her back, and said, “Won’t you come home with me in the carriage?

sentences.zh: 」夫人不顧，又不應。

translations.literal: " The lady did not turn her head and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” She neither looked at him nor replied.

sentences.zh: 太祖却行，立於戶外，復云：「得無尚可邪！

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor stepped backward, stood outside the door, and said again, "Could it still be all right!
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the threshold and called, “Is there still no way to patch this?

sentences.zh: 」遂不應，太祖曰：「真訣矣。

translations.literal: " Still she did not answer, and the Grand Progenitor said, "It is truly over.
translations.idiomatic: ” Again she was silent, and he said, “Then it is finished between us.

sentences.zh: 」遂與絕，欲其家嫁之，其家不敢。

translations.literal: " He broke with her and wished her family to marry her off, but her family did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: ” He severed ties and wanted her kin to remarry her, yet they dared not.

sentences.zh: 初，丁夫人旣爲嫡，加有子脩，丁視后母子不足。

translations.literal: At first, once Lady Ding had been principal wife and moreover had son Xiu, Lady Ding regarded the empress and her children as beneath notice.
translations.idiomatic: While Lady Ding was still principal consort and mother to Cao Ang, she looked down on Lady Bian and her sons.

sentences.zh: 后爲繼室，不念舊惡，因太祖出行，常四時使人饋遺，又私迎之，延以正坐而己下之，迎來送去，有如昔日。

translations.literal: After the empress became successor wife she did not remember old wrongs; whenever the Grand Progenitor traveled she regularly sent seasonal gifts in all four seasons, and also privately welcomed her, seated her in the seat of honor while placing herself below, escorting her coming and going as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lady Bian became principal wife she refused to nurse old grudges. Whenever Cao Cao was away she sent seasonal gifts, received Lady Ding in private, gave her the host’s seat while taking a lower place herself, and saw her off and welcomed her as in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 丁謝曰：「廢放之人，夫人何能常爾邪！

translations.literal: Lady Ding declined, saying, "I am a cast-off person—how can you always treat me thus!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding protested, “I am a discarded woman—why should you honor me like this?

sentences.zh: 」其後丁亡，后請太祖殯葬，許之，乃葬許城南。

translations.literal: " Later when Lady Ding died the empress asked the Grand Progenitor for a funeral; he granted it, and she was buried south of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: ” After Lady Ding died, Lady Bian begged Cao Cao to bury her properly; he agreed, and she was interred south of Xu.

sentences.zh: 後太祖病困，自慮不起，歎曰：「我前後行意，於心未曾有所負也。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Progenitor was gravely ill and feared he would not recover, he sighed, "In all I have done before and after, my heart has never knowingly wronged anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Cao Cao lay dying, he sighed, “In everything I have done I do not believe I ever knowingly betrayed another.

sentences.zh: 假令死而有靈，子脩若問『我母所在』，我將何辭以荅！

translations.literal: Suppose that after death there is awareness and son Xiu asks, 'Where is my mother?'—what words could I use to answer!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the dead have awareness and Cao Ang asks where his mother is, what answer could I give?

sentences.zh: 」《魏書》曰：后性約儉，不尚華麗，無文繡珠玉，器皆黑漆。

translations.literal: " The Book of Wei states: The empress’s nature was frugal and restrained; she did not esteem splendor and finery; there were no patterned silks or pearls and jade; vessels were all black lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Book of Wei adds that Lady Bian lived plainly—no embroidered silks or jade ornaments, only black-lacquer ware.

sentences.zh: 太祖常得名璫數具，命后自選一具，后取其中者，太祖問其故，對曰：「取其上者爲貪，取其下者爲偽，故取其中者。」〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once obtained several fine pearl hairpins and ordered the empress to choose one; she took those of middle quality, and when the Grand Progenitor asked the reason she replied, "To take the best would be greed; to take the lowest would be pretense; therefore I take the middle ones."〉
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao offered her a choice of jeweled pins she picked middling ones, explaining, “The finest would show greed, the poorest affectation; the middle course is honest.”〉

sentences.zh: 文帝爲太子，左右長御賀后曰：「將軍拜太子，天下莫不歡喜，后當傾府藏賞賜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was heir apparent, the chief women attendants congratulated the empress, saying, "The general has been invested as heir; none under heaven fails to rejoice—the empress ought to empty the treasury stores to reward and bestow.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi became heir, his senior maids told Lady Bian, “The heir has been named; the whole realm rejoices. You should fling open the treasuries and give largesse.

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「王自以丕年大，故用爲嗣，我但當以免無教導之過爲幸耳，亦何爲當重賜遺乎！

translations.literal: " The empress said, "The king appointed Pi heir because of his age; I should count myself fortunate merely to escape blame for failing to instruct him—why should there be heavy gifts and largesse!
translations.idiomatic: ” She answered, “The king chose Pi because he is the elder son. I am lucky enough not to be faulted for poor upbringing—why heap rewards on everyone?

sentences.zh: 」長御還，具以語太祖。

translations.literal: " The chief attendants returned and reported everything to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: ” They reported her words to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖恱曰：「怒不變容，喜不失節，故是最爲難。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said, "Not to change countenance in anger nor lose measure in joy—therein lies what is hardest."
translations.idiomatic: He said with satisfaction, “To stay calm in anger and measured in joy—that is the rarest thing of all.”

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜爲王后，策曰：「夫人卞氏，撫養諸子，有母儀之德。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year she was invested as queen; the patent read, "Lady Bian has reared the various sons and possesses the virtue of a motherly model.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian’an she was enfeoffed as queen. The edict read, “Lady Bian has nurtured the princes and embodies a mother’s standard.

sentences.zh: 今進位王后，太子諸侯陪位，羣卿上壽，減國內死罪一等。

translations.literal: Now we advance her to queen; the heir apparent and feudal lords shall attend in support, the ministers shall offer longevity toasts, and capital crimes within the realm are reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore raise her to queen; the heir and feudal lords shall attend while ministers toast her long life, and death sentences across the domain are commuted one degree.

sentences.zh: 」二十五年，太祖崩，文帝即王位，尊后曰王太后，及踐阼，尊后曰皇太后，稱永壽宮。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fifth year the Grand Progenitor died; Emperor Wen assumed the king’s position, honored the empress as Queen Dowager, and when he ascended the throne honored her as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yongshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next year Cao Cao died. Cao Pi, now king, styled her Queen Dowager, and as emperor raised her to Empress Dowager of Yongshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后以國用不足，滅損御食，諸金銀器物皆去之。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: Because state funds were insufficient the empress reduced palace meals and removed all gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that she cut palace meals when the treasury ran short and stripped the kitchens of gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 東阿王植，太后少子，最愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Dong'e Zhi was the empress dowager’s youngest son and the one she loved most.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, prince of Dong’e, was her youngest and her favorite.

sentences.zh: 後植犯法，爲有司所奏，文帝令太后弟子奉車都尉蘭持公卿議白太后，太后曰：「不意此兒所作如是，汝還語帝，不可以我故壞國法。

translations.literal: Later when Zhi violated the law and was impeached by the responsible officials, Emperor Wen ordered the empress dowager’s nephew Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Lan to present the deliberations of the dukes and ministers to the empress dowager; the empress dowager said, "I never expected this child to act thus; you return and tell the emperor that he must not, for my sake, damage the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Zhi broke the law and officials impeached him, Wen-di sent her nephew Lan, commandant of the imperial carriage, with the ministers’ verdict. She said only, “I never thought this boy would go so far. Go back and tell the Son of Heaven not to bend the statutes for my sake.

sentences.zh: 」及自見帝，不以爲言。

translations.literal: " When she herself saw the emperor she did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: ” When she next saw the emperor she never raised the matter.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：文帝夢磨錢，欲使文滅而更愈明，以問周宣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Emperor Wen dreamed of grinding cash, wishing the inscription to wear away yet it grew clearer; he asked Zhou Xuan about it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: Wen-di dreamed of grinding coins, wanting the characters to fade yet they grew sharper, and asked Zhou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣荅曰：「此陛下家事，雖意欲爾，而太后不聽。

translations.literal: Xuan replied, "This is a household matter of Your Majesty; though you may wish it so, the empress dowager will not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan answered, “This concerns your own household: though you wish one outcome, the empress dowager will not consent.

sentences.zh: 」則太后用意，不得如此書所言也。

translations.literal: " Then the empress dowager’s intent cannot have been as this text describes.
translations.idiomatic: ” So her attitude cannot have matched what this passage claims.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》又曰：太后每隨軍征行，見高年白首，輙住車呼問，賜與絹帛，對之涕泣曰：「恨父母不及我時也。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei also states: Whenever the empress dowager followed the army on campaign and saw white-haired elders she would halt the carriage, call out to ask after them, and grant silk and cloth; facing them with tears she said, "I regret that my parents did not reach my time.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei also says that on campaign she stopped her carriage for white-haired villagers, gave them silk, and wept, “I mourn that my own parents never lived to see days like these.

sentences.zh: 」太后每見外親，不假以顏色，常言「居處當務節儉，不當望賞賜，念自佚也。

translations.literal: " Whenever the empress dowager saw outer kin she did not relax her stern countenance and often said, "In dwelling one must practice frugality; one should not expect rewards and largesse or think only of ease.
translations.idiomatic: ” To kinsmen from outside the palace she showed no easy warmth, warning, “Live modestly; do not look for gifts or live only for comfort.

sentences.zh: 外舍當怪吾遇之太薄，吾自有常度故也。

translations.literal: Those outside will surely wonder that I treat them too coldly—I have my constant measure for it.
translations.idiomatic: They may think me harsh, but I keep to my rule.

sentences.zh: 吾事武帝四五十年，行儉日久，不能自變爲奢，有犯科禁者，吾且能加罪一等耳，莫望錢米恩貸也。

translations.literal: I have served Emperor Wu four or five decades and have long practiced austerity; I cannot suddenly turn extravagant; if anyone breaks the statutes I can only add one degree to the penalty—do not expect cash or grain indulgence from me.
translations.idiomatic: I served Emperor Wu forty or fifty years in frugal habit; I will not turn lavish now. Whoever breaks the law gets an extra degree of punishment from me—never expect money or grain favors.

sentences.zh: 」帝爲太后弟秉起第，第成，太后幸第請諸家外親，設下廚，無異膳。

translations.literal: " The emperor built a mansion for the empress dowager’s younger brother Bing; when it was finished the empress dowager visited the mansion and invited the various outer kin, setting out a lower kitchen with no unusual delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ming-di built a mansion for her brother Bing; when she toured it she feasted the kin with plain fare from the lower kitchen, nothing special.

sentences.zh: 太后左右菜食粟飯，無魚肉。

translations.literal: Those to the empress dowager’s left and right ate vegetable fare and millet rice, with no fish or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Her own attendants ate vegetables and millet, no meat or fish.

sentences.zh: 其儉如此。〉

translations.literal: Her frugality was thus.〉
translations.idiomatic: Such was her austerity.〉

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，尊太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming-di succeeded he raised her to Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，文帝欲追封太后父母，尚書陳羣奏曰：「陛下以聖德應運受命，創業革制，當永爲後式。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era Emperor Wen wished posthumously to enfeoff the empress dowager’s parents; Minister of the Secretariat Chen Qun submitted, "Your Majesty, endowed with sagely virtue, has received the mandate, founded the enterprise, and reformed institutions; you should forever be a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu, Wen-di wanted to posthumously ennoble Lady Bian’s parents. Chen Qun objected: “You received the mandate with sage virtue and set new institutions—you must be the pattern for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 案典籍之文，無婦人分土命爵之制。

translations.literal: Examining the texts of the canons, there is no system by which a woman is granted land or a noble title.
translations.idiomatic: The classics nowhere grant women fiefs or noble rank of their own.

sentences.zh: 在禮典，婦因夫爵。

translations.literal: In the ritual canons a woman takes rank through her husband.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual gives a wife rank only through her husband.

sentences.zh: 秦違古法，漢氏因之，非先王之令典也。

translations.literal: Qin violated the ancient pattern; Han continued it—it is not the canonical model of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Qin broke the ancient rule and Han followed suit; neither matches the true kings’ code.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此議是也，其勿施行。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "This opinion is correct; do not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor agreed: “Do not enact it.

sentences.zh: 以作著詔下藏之臺閣，永爲後式。

translations.literal: Draw up an edict recording this, deposit it in the archives, and let it be a model forever.
translations.idiomatic: Instead promulgate an edict, file it in the tower archives, and let it stand forever as precedent.

sentences.zh: 」至太和四年春，明帝乃追謚太后祖父廣曰開陽恭侯，父遠曰敬侯，祖母周封陽都君及敬侯夫人，皆贈印綬。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the fourth year of Taihe Emperor Ming posthumously honored the empress dowager’s grandfather Guang as Marquis Gong of Kaiyang, her father Yuan as Marquis Jing, her grandmother Zhou as Mistress of Yangdu and the Lady of Marquis Jing, all with seals and ribbons conferred.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Taihe 4 Ming-di belatedly ennobled her grandfather Guang as Marquis Gong of Kaiyang, her father Yuan as Marquis Jing, and her grandmother Zhou as lady of Yangdu and consort of Marquis Jing, each with seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，后崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: She died that fifth month.

sentences.zh: 七月，合葬高陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month she was jointly buried at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month she was laid beside Cao Cao in the Gaoling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 文昭甄皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wen-Zhao, née Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-Zhao of the Zhen clan

sentences.zh: 景初元年夏，有司議定七廟。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jingchu the responsible officials deliberated fixing the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 (237 CE) officials debated the arrangement of the seven imperial temples.

sentences.zh: 冬，又奏曰：「蓋帝王之興，既有受命之君，又有聖妃協於神靈，然後克昌厥世，以成王業焉。

translations.literal: In winter they again submitted: "The rise of an emperor and king always has both the lord who receives the mandate and the sagely consort who harmonizes with the spirits; only then can his age flourish and the royal enterprise be completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they memorialized: “Every dynastic founder has both the ruler who receives the mandate and the consort who answers heaven; only then does the house flourish and the great work stand complete.

sentences.zh: 昔高辛氏卜其四妃之子皆有天下，而帝摯、陶唐、商、周代興。

translations.literal: In antiquity Gaoxin divined among the sons of his four consorts and each possessed the realm, while Di Zhi, Tao Tang, Shang, and Zhou rose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: High antiquity saw Gaoxin divine which of his four wives’ sons would rule; lines descended through Di Zhi, Yao’s house, Shang, and Zhou each rose in turn.

sentences.zh: 週人上推后稷，以配皇天，追述王初，本之姜嫄，特立宮廟，世世享嘗，周禮所謂『奏夷則，歌中呂，舞大濩，以享先妣』者也。

translations.literal: The Zhou people traced their line to Hou Ji to match August Heaven; pursuing the kingly beginning to its root in Jiang Yuan they established a separate palace temple, generation after generation enjoying sacrifice—what the Rites of Zhou calls 'performing the yi mode, singing the zhong lü mode, dancing the Great Hu to honor the first mother.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou looked back to Hou Ji to pair with High Heaven and, tracing their kings to Jiang Yuan, set her a special temple where each generation offered sacrifice—what the Rites of Zhou means by honoring the founding mother with music and dance.

sentences.zh: 詩人頌之曰：『厥初生民，時維姜嫄。

translations.literal: The poets praise it, saying, 'The first birth of the people—this was Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes sing, “The birth of the people began from Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 』言王化之本，生民所由。

translations.literal: ' It speaks of the root of kingly transformation and the source from which the people come.
translations.idiomatic: ” That is the taproot of royal civilizing power and of the people themselves.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『閟宮有侐，實實枚枚，赫赫姜嫄，其德不回。

translations.literal: It also says, 'The temple of Bi is solemn; truly solid, truly thick; splendidly august is Jiang Yuan, whose virtue does not waver.
translations.idiomatic: They add, “Bi’s shrine stands in awe, firm and ample; august Jiang Yuan’s virtue never falters.

sentences.zh: 』詩、禮所稱姬宗之盛，其美如此。

translations.literal: ' What the Odes and Rites praise of the Ji clan’s splendor is thus beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: ” So the canonical texts glorify the Ji house.

sentences.zh: 大魏期運，繼於有虞，然崇弘帝道，三世彌隆，廟祧之數，實與周同。

translations.literal: Great Wei’s allotted fortune succeeds that of Youyu, yet in exalting the imperial way three reigns have grown ever more glorious; the number of temples to be shifted matches Zhou’s.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s mandate follows Shun’s line, yet across three reigns the imperial way has only deepened; the temple shifts now contemplated mirror Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 今武宣皇后、文德皇后各配無窮之祚，至於文昭皇后膺天靈符，誕育明聖​​，功濟生民，德盈宇宙，開諸後嗣，乃道化之所興也。

translations.literal: Now Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan and Empress Wen-De each match an endless blessing; as for Empress Wen-Zhao, she received heaven’s talisman, bore the enlightened sage, aided the living people, filled the cosmos with virtue, and opened the way for later heirs—she is what the transforming way exalts.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Dowager Wu-Xuan and Wen-De already receive perpetual pairing rites; Empress Wen-Zhao bore the sage heir, succored the people, and filled heaven and earth with merit—she is the mother in whom the moral order itself is renewed.

sentences.zh: 寢廟特祀，亦姜嫄之閟宮也，而未著不毀之制，懼論功報德之義，萬世或闕焉，非所以昭孝示後世也。

translations.literal: A separate temple sacrifice is also like Jiang Yuan’s temple of Bi, yet the system of non-destruction has not been clarified; I fear the meaning of repaying merit and virtue may across myriad ages sometimes be wanting—this is not how to display filial piety and show later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Her shrine deserves singular rites like Jiang Yuan’s, yet we have not fixed the rule that her temple never be dismantled; I fear posterity might slight the duty to repay her deeds. That would ill serve filial display for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 文昭廟宜世世享祀奏樂，與祖廟同，永著不毀之典，以播聖善之風。

translations.literal: The temple of Empress Wen-Zhao should receive sacrifice with music performed generation after generation, the same as the ancestor temples; eternally establish the norm of non-destruction, so as to spread the wind of sagely goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-Zhao’s temple ought to receive music and offerings in every generation on the same footing as the founding shrines, fixing forever the rule that it never be dismantled so her sanctity may shine for ages.

sentences.zh: 」於是與七廟議並勒金策，藏之金匱。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together with the deliberation on the seven temples it was inscribed on a golden document and stored in a golden coffer.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court then had this, together with the seven-temples decision, engraved on gold slips and laid them in the golden coffer.

sentences.zh: 文德郭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wen-De, née Guo
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-De of the Guo clan

sentences.zh: 后早喪兄弟，以從兄表繼永後，拜奉車都尉。

translations.literal: The empress had early lost her brothers; she took her cousin Biao to continue Yong’s posterity and invested him as Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After her brothers died young, she had her cousin Guo Biao posthumously continue another brother’s line and appointed him commandant of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 后外親劉斐與他國為婚，后聞之，敕曰：「諸親戚嫁娶，自當與鄉里門戶匹敵者，不得因勢，強與他方人婚也。

translations.literal: When an outer kinsman of the empress, Liu Fei, contracted a marriage with another state, the empress heard of it and instructed, saying, "In the marriages of our kin they naturally ought to match families of comparable standing in their own villages and gates; they must not rely on power to force unions with people from distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: When a relative by marriage, Liu Fei, allied his house with another kingdom, she issued an order: “Our kinsmen’s weddings should pair like with like in their own neighborhoods; no one may use influence to drag in spouses from far away.

sentences.zh: 」后姊子孟武還鄉里，求小妻，后止之。

translations.literal: " Her elder sister’s son Meng Wu returned to his home region seeking a concubine; the empress stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: ” She also blocked her sister’s son Meng Wu when he went home looking for a secondary wife.

sentences.zh: 遂敕諸家曰：「今世婦女少，當配將士，不得因緣取以為妾也。

translations.literal: Thereupon she instructed the various families, saying, "In the present age women are few; they ought to be given in marriage to soldiers and officers; you must not seize pretexts to take them as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: She then warned every branch of the clan: “Women are scarce in wartime; they belong with the troops. Do not invent excuses to press them into concubinage.

sentences.zh: 宜各自慎，無為罰首。」

translations.literal: Each should be cautious on his own account and not be the first to incur punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Watch yourselves—do not be the first to bring down the law.”

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后常敕戒表、武等曰：「漢氏椒房之家，少能自全者，皆由驕奢，可不慎乎！」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: The empress often admonished Biao, Wu, and the like, saying, "Among the pepper-chamber houses of Han, few could preserve themselves—all because of arrogance and extravagance; can one not be cautious!"〉
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei adds that she repeatedly cautioned Guo Biao, Meng Wu, and their circle: “Few consort clans under Han survived their own pride and waste—take care.”〉

sentences.zh: 五年，帝東征，后留許昌永始台。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor campaigned east; the empress remained at Yongshi Terrace in Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of an era (Huangchu) the emperor marched east while she stayed at Yongshi Terrace in Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 時霖雨百餘日，城樓多壞，有司奏請移止。

translations.literal: At that time there was unbroken rain for more than a hundred days; many city towers were damaged, and the responsible officials memorialized asking to move her lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for over a hundred days straight, ruining tower works, so officials begged her to relocate.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「昔楚昭王出遊，貞姜留漸台，江水至，使者迎而無符，不去，卒沒。

translations.literal: The empress said, "In antiquity when King Zhao of Chu traveled abroad, the chaste Lady Jiang remained on the Gradual Terrace; when the river rose the messenger came to fetch her but lacked the tally, so she would not leave and at last drowned.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “Long ago, when King Zhao of Chu was away, his faithful Jiang stayed on the Gradual Terrace; the river rose, yet without the proper tally she refused to flee and drowned.

sentences.zh: 今帝在遠，吾幸未有是患，而便移止，奈何？

translations.literal: Now the emperor is far away; I have fortunately not yet met with that calamity—yet I should move lodging—how could that be right?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is far off, and I have no such flood at my door—why should I bolt at the first leak?

sentences.zh: 」群臣莫敢復言。

translations.literal: " None of the ministers dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: ” No minister dared press the point again.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝東征吳，至廣陵，后留譙宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor campaigned east against Wu, reaching Guangling; the empress remained at the palace in Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he campaigned east against Wu as far as Guangling, leaving her at the Qiao palace.

sentences.zh: 時表留宿衛，欲遏水取魚。

translations.literal: At that time Biao remained on night guard and wished to dam water to catch fish.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Biao, left on night duty, wanted to block a stream to seine for fish.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「水噹通運漕，又少材木，奴客不在目前，當複私取官竹木作梁遏。

translations.literal: The empress said, "The water ought to remain open for the transport canal; moreover timber is scarce; the slaves and retainers are not before one’s eyes—would one again privately take official bamboo and timber to make beams for a dam?
translations.idiomatic: She reproved him: “That water feeds the supply barges, and lumber is short. Your servants are not here to haul timber—would you raid government bamboo to brace a private weir?

sentences.zh: 今奉車所不足者，豈魚乎？」

translations.literal: What the commandant of the carriage lacks—is it fish?"
translations.idiomatic: Is the commandant of the carriage short of fish?”

sentences.zh: 明悼毛皇后

translations.literal: Empress Ming-Dao of the Mao clan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ming-Dao, née Mao

sentences.zh: 明悼毛皇后，河內人也。

translations.literal: Empress Ming-Dao, née Mao, was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao, honored as Empress Ming-Dao, came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，以選入東宮，明帝時為平原王，進御有寵，出入與同輿輦。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era she was selected into the Eastern Palace; when Emperor Ming was Prince of Pingyuan she attended his bed and had favor, going out and in in the same carriage and palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu she entered the heir’s residence; while the future Ming-di was still prince of Pingyuan she won his favor and rode with him in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 及即帝立，以為貴嬪。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne and was established as emperor he made her Honored Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne he raised her to Honored Concubine.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 后父​​嘉，拜騎都尉，后弟曾，郎中。

translations.literal: The empress’s father Jia was appointed Cavalry Commandant; her younger brother Zeng, Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Mao Jia became cavalry commandant; her brother Mao Zeng, a gentleman at court.

sentences.zh: 帝之幸郭元后也，后愛寵日弛。

translations.literal: When the emperor favored Lady Guo who would be empress with the Yuan title, the empress’s love and favor daily slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ming-di’s affection shifted to Lady Guo—the future Empress Yuan—Lady Mao’s favor ebbed by the day.

sentences.zh: 景初元年，帝遊后園，召才人以上曲宴極樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu the emperor toured the rear garden and summoned concubines of Talent rank and above to a winding banquet with utmost merriment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 he held a private revel in the rear park with every consort from Talent upward.

sentences.zh: 元后曰「宜延皇后」，帝弗許。

translations.literal: The Yuan empress said, "You ought to invite the empress"; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo urged him to send for the empress; he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃禁左右，使不得宣。

translations.literal: He then silenced those around him so they could not announce it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to keep silent so word would not reach her.

sentences.zh: 后知之，明日，帝見后，后曰：「昨日遊宴北園，樂乎？

translations.literal: When the empress learned of it, the next day when the emperor saw the empress she said, "Yesterday you feasted in the north garden—was it pleasant?
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he came to her apartments, she asked calmly, “Was the north-garden party yesterday to your liking?

sentences.zh: 」帝以左右洩之，所殺十餘人。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because those at his side had leaked it, killed more than ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: ” Enraged that someone had told her, he executed over a dozen people.

sentences.zh: 賜后死，然猶加諡，葬愍陵。

translations.literal: He granted the empress death, yet still added a posthumous title and buried her at Min Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He then forced her to take her own life, yet still granted a posthumous name and buried her at the Mausoleum of Lament.

sentences.zh: 遷曾散騎常侍，後徙為羽林虎賁中郎將、原武典農。

translations.literal: Zeng was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, later transferred to Colonel of the Feathered Forest Tiger Guards and Director of Agriculture for Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zeng was moved up to regular attendant at court, then to colonel of the feathered forest guards and overseer of the Yuanwu agricultural colony.

sentences.zh: 明元郭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Ming-Yuan of the Guo clan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ming-Yuan, née Guo

translations.literal: 【Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 評曰：魏后妃之家，雖云富貴，未有若衰漢乘非其據，宰割朝政者也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Among the families of Wei’s empresses and consorts, though they are called rich and noble, none seized illegitimate position and carved up court government as did the declining Han.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict: Wei’s consort clans grew wealthy, yet none usurped the government the way late Han favorites did.

sentences.zh: 鑑往易軌，於斯為美。

translations.literal: Taking the past as a mirror and changing the track—herein lies the good.
translations.idiomatic: They learned from history and kept to a safer path—that is the virtue here.

sentences.zh: 追觀陳群之議，棧潛之論，適足以為百王之規典，垂憲範乎後葉矣。

translations.literal: Looking back at Chen Qun’s memorial and Zhan Qian’s discourse, they suffice to be a normative model for a hundred kings and to hang a legal pattern before later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in hindsight, Chen Qun’s memorial and Zhan Qian’s admonitions are enough to serve as precedent for any line of kings and to hand down a pattern of law for generations yet to come.
